title: How to write an estimate for an electrical panel upgrade
summary: Paste your panel-upgrade notes into ChatGPT and get a clear estimate. Check the price and the permit line before you send it, and do not invent an amperage.

tests.prompt:
You help an electrician write an estimate for an electrical panel upgrade. Draft only. Do not send it.

Fill in these details. If a line is blank, write UNKNOWN and do not guess.

Customer name: [CUSTOMER NAME]
Job address: [JOB ADDRESS]
Current panel and service, if known: [CURRENT PANEL]
What's wrong or why it needs upgrading: [REASON]
Recommended work: [WORK]
Permit and inspection, if included: [PERMIT]
Price: [PRICE]
What's included: [INCLUDED]
What's not included: [NOT INCLUDED]
How long the work takes: [TIME ON SITE]
How long the estimate is good: [EXPIRATION]
Your name and business: [YOUR NAME]
Your phone: [YOUR PHONE]
Email or text: [CHANNEL]

Rules:
- Never invent details; if something is missing, ask or mark it UNKNOWN.
- Do not invent an amperage, a brand, a permit fee, or a rebate.
- Do not say the panel is unsafe or a fire risk unless those words are already in [REASON].
- Do not change [PRICE]. Copy it exactly.
- Keep the tone plain and steady. No pressure.
- If permit language is blank, mark PERMIT UNKNOWN. Do not assume a permit is included.

Output format:
Return these headings only:
Channel
Subject (NONE if this is a text)
Estimate (200 words or fewer for email, 100 words or fewer for a text)
The situation
The work
Price
What's included
What's not included
Next step
Facts used

setup.agent: Paste this into ChatGPT, or into the chat assistant you already use.
steps: Write the customer name, address, the current panel if you know it, why it needs upgrading, the work you recommend, and whether a permit and inspection are included.
Add the price, what's included and not, time on site, how long the estimate is good, your name, phone, and the channel.
Open ChatGPT, paste the ChatGPT prompt, and replace every [BRACKET]. Type UNKNOWN if you have not confirmed the amperage or the permit yet.
Check the work, the price, and the permit line against your notes. Delete any safety scare, rebate, or brand you did not write down.
Paste the estimate into email or a text and send it yourself.
setup.approvalStep: You check the recommended work, the price, and whether the permit is included, then you send the estimate yourself.
failureModes: The draft invents an amperage, a panel brand, or a rebate. Put only your notes back in.
The wording says the panel is a fire hazard when you did not say that. Keep the reason factual.
The permit is described as included when you left that line blank. Mark it UNKNOWN or add your real permit terms.
The price does not match your quote. Copy your number exactly.

faq.q: I have not confirmed whether a permit is required. What should I do?
faq.a: Leave the permit line blank so the draft marks it UNKNOWN. Confirm with the local building department, then add whether the permit and inspection are included before you send the estimate.

faq.q: Should I mention that the power will be off?
faq.a: Yes, if that is true for the job. Homeowners need to plan for it. Put the power-off window in your notes so it shows up in the estimate.

faq.q: Can I include a surge protector as an option?
faq.a: You can list it under What's not included and offer a separate price later, or run a second estimate for that add-on. Do not bury an extra charge in this total.

job: Paste panel-upgrade notes and get a clear estimate a homeowner can approve.
who: Electricians and electrical contractors who quote panel upgrades and want a plain estimate that does not invent technical details.

example.scenario: An electrician is quoting a 100-amp to 200-amp panel upgrade for a homeowner who is adding a range and a dryer.
example.input:
Customer name: Avery Kim
Job address: 77 Stone Avenue
Current panel and service, if known: 100-amp panel, full
What's wrong or why it needs upgrading: The panel is full, and the new range and dryer need more capacity
Recommended work: Install a 200-amp service and a new 200-amp panel
Permit and inspection, if included: Permit and inspection are included
Price: $4,200
What's included: New 200-amp panel, meter base as required, grounding, labeling, and the city permit and inspection
What's not included: New circuits inside the house, a whole-home surge device, and drywall repair
How long the work takes: One day, power off for several hours
How long the estimate is good: 30 days
Your name and business: Taylor at Bright Path Electric
Your phone: 555-0117
Email or text: email
example.output:
Channel: email
Subject: Panel upgrade estimate for 77 Stone Avenue

Estimate:
Hi Avery, this is Taylor at Bright Path Electric. Here is the estimate to upgrade the electrical panel at 77 Stone Avenue.

The situation: The current 100-amp panel is full, and the new range and dryer need more capacity.

The work: Install a 200-amp service and a new 200-amp panel. The power will be off for several hours, and the work takes one day.

Price: $4,200. This estimate is good for 30 days.

What's included: The new 200-amp panel, the meter base as required, grounding, labeling, and the city permit and inspection.

What's not included: New circuits inside the house, a whole-home surge device, and drywall repair.

Next step: Reply or call 555-0117 if you would like to book, and I will walk you through the power-off window before we set a date.

Facts used: 77 Stone Avenue, 100-amp to 200-amp, $4,200, permit included, 30 days.
Unknown: none.
example.notes: Made-up job details, only to show a clear panel-upgrade estimate.
